sources.entry: OO vs FP, Robert C. Martin, The Clean Code Blog. A pretty interesting take on the differences between OOP and FP from an expert in OOP.

summary.title: FPvsOO: OO vs FP (The Clean Code Blog)
summary.one_liner: Robert C. Martin argues that OO and FP are not mutually exclusive: OO is about function polymorphism rather than state, FP imposes discipline on assignment, and the two can be combined.
takeaways: Objects are better seen as bags of functions than bags of data; hiding state is central to OO.
Both OO and FP are composed of functions operating on data; the difference lies in discipline around assignment (FP) and function pointers (OO).
Polymorphism's main benefit is inverting source code dependencies, which enables plugin architectures.
Avoiding assignment reduces concurrent update problems, making functional programs safer in multiprocessing.
OO and FP are not mutually exclusive; design principles and patterns apply regardless of paradigm.
summary.summary: A blog essay by Robert C. Martin responding to a claim that OO and FP are mutually exclusive. He argues from first principles, distinguishing FP's discipline on assignment from OO's discipline on function pointers, and explains that polymorphism enables dependency inversion and plugin architectures. He also notes immutability's concurrency benefits. The post is opinionated and short, using informal examples and footnotes rather than code benchmarks.
